title: Ontario Business Registry Filing Checker | What Goes There
content:
Registry

Ontario Business Registry Filing Checker

The annual return, address changes and director changes are filed through the Ontario Business Registry. None of them is the T2.

Four answersRegistry filings onlyNot part of the T2Corporation number needed

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

What the registry may be waiting for

Answer the four questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What the Ontario Business Registry Is For

The Ontario Business Registry is the provincial system through which the annual return, address changes and director changes are filed. A corporation needs its Ontario corporation number and its registry access to use it.

It is not where tax is filed. The T2 goes to the Canada Revenue Agency, and the two trails are independent: a corporation can be fully current on its T2 filings and still be out of date at the registry.

What Goes to Which Body

FilingFiled withCarries tax
The Ontario annual returnThe Ontario Business RegistryNo. It carries no tax and no payment
A change of registered office addressThe Ontario Business RegistryNo
A change of directors or officersThe Ontario Business RegistryNo
The T2 corporate returnThe Canada Revenue AgencyYes, where there is tax to carry

The annual return versus tax return checker separates the two filings, and the Ontario annual return versus the T2 sets them side by side.

Nothing in the T2 Prompts the Registry Filing

Until 2021 the Ontario annual return was filed alongside the T2, so one act covered both. Since October 2021 it is filed through the Ontario Business Registry instead.

Because the filing moved out of the T2, nothing in the corporate tax return now prompts an owner to do it. The prompt has to come from the owner or the adviser, which is the whole reason this checker exists.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is filed through the Ontario Business Registry?

The annual return, changes of registered office address and changes of directors or officers. The T2 is not: it goes to the Canada Revenue Agency.

What do I need to use the registry?

The corporation’s Ontario corporation number and its registry access. Without those, none of the filings can be made.

Is any of this included in nil T2 filing?

No. Registry filings are not part of nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, and filing the T2 does not satisfy an annual return.

Does filing the T2 update the registry?

No. The two go to different bodies and neither carries anything to the other. A registry record stays exactly as it was until a registry filing changes it.

What goes wrong when the registered office address is stale?

Mail stops arriving anywhere anyone reads it. That includes the notice warning that the corporation is about to be struck for a missed annual return, which is the one letter an owner most needs to see.

A director has resigned. What do I file?

A change of directors, through the registry. It is its own filing, separate from the annual return, and it is reported nowhere on the corporate tax return.

Does a dormant corporation have to keep any of this current?

Yes. The registry asks who the directors are and where the office is, and those answers are owed whether or not the corporation traded in the year.

Who is allowed to make these filings?

Someone with authority to bind the corporation, which in practice means a director or an officer. An adviser can file on instructions, but the authority still comes from inside the corporation.

Does the registry pass anything to the Canada Revenue Agency?

No. The two keep separate records and neither reports a filing status to the other, so being current in one place proves nothing about the other.

Is a numbered company treated any differently?

No. A number instead of a name changes nothing about which filings are owed or when they fall due.

title: Schedule 546 Checker | Does the T2 Still Carry It
content:
Registry

Schedule 546 Ontario Annual Return Checker

The Ontario annual return travelled with the T2 until 2021 and goes through the Ontario Business Registry from October 2021.

One date inDates the cutoverOctober 2021Separate filing now

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Which tax year

Enter the tax year-end above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Changed in October 2021

Until 2021 the Ontario annual return was filed alongside the T2. Since October 2021 it is filed through the Ontario Business Registry instead, and a corporation that has not looked at the rules since then is probably not filing it.

That is the whole of it. The filing did not go away and it did not change what it reports: it changed where it goes, and the T2 stopped carrying it.

The Two Routes, Either Side of the Cutover

Tax year endingWhere the annual return wentWhat prompted it
Before October 2021Alongside the T2Preparing the T2, because the two travelled together
From October 2021Through the Ontario Business RegistryNothing in the T2. The prompt has to come from the owner or the adviser

The Ontario Business Registry filing checker names what else goes through the registry.

The Annual Return Is Still Owed Either Way

An annual return confirms the registered office address, the directors and the officers, and it carries no tax and no payment. An annual return is not a tax filing, so having no income does not excuse it.

So a dormant corporation owes one for every year, on whichever route applied to that year. Filing the T2 does not satisfy it, and filing it does not satisfy the T2.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the T2 still carry the Ontario annual return?

Not for a tax year ending from October 2021. Until 2021 it was filed alongside the T2; since then it goes through the Ontario Business Registry.

Why do people still think it travels with the T2?

Because it did until 2021, and because nothing in the corporate tax return now prompts an owner to file it separately.

Does a dormant corporation still owe one?

Yes. An annual return confirms directors and the registered office rather than income, so having no activity does not excuse it.

What was Schedule 546?

The Ontario annual return in the form it took while it travelled with the T2: a schedule inside the corporate tax return rather than a filing of its own.

My tax year straddles the change. Which route applies?

The calculator reads the year-end, because the year-end is what dates the return. Enter it above and it names the route that applied to that year.

Did what the annual return asks for change as well?

No. It confirms the directors and the registered office either way. What changed is where it is filed, and that it is no longer part of the tax return.

My accountant files the T2. Does that cover it?

Not for a year ending from October 2021. Once the schedule left the return, filing the T2 stopped producing an annual return, and nothing in the return now prompts anyone to file one.

Is the Ontario annual return inside the filing fee?

No. Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the corporate tax return. An annual return is a registry filing and sits outside it.

Can an annual return that was missed still be filed?

An outstanding annual return goes through the registry whichever year it belongs to. How many are outstanding is a separate question, and the missed annual returns calculator counts them.

Does a skipped year before 2021 matter now?

It leaves the registry record out of date for that year. An annual return that was never filed stays unfiled, and a later one does not stand in for it.

title: Ontario Missed Annual Returns | How Many Are Outstanding
content:
Registry

Ontario Missed Annual Returns Calculator

One annual return falls due for each tax year. Enter the year-end of the last one filed to count what is outstanding since.

One date inCounts the yearsRegistry record onlySeparate from the T2

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

The last annual return filed

Enter the tax year-end of the last annual return filed.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Annual Return for Each Tax Year

The Ontario annual return is tied to the tax year-end, so one falls due for each tax year the corporation exists. Missing a year does not remove it: the next year adds its own, and they accumulate.

An annual return is not a tax filing, so having no income does not excuse it. A dormant corporation confirms its directors and its registered office every year in exactly the way an active one does.

What a Missed Year Actually Causes

MissedWhat it createsWhat it does not create
One annual returnA registry record that is out of dateAny tax
Several annual returnsA corporation the registry treats as abandonedAny tax
Enough of themA registry that may dissolve or strike the corporationDissolution for tax purposes, and it cancels no outstanding T2 return

The involuntary dissolution risk checker takes being struck, and the corporate revival requirement checker takes what happens after it.

The Registry Count and the Tax Count Are Separate

The two trails are independent. A corporation can be fully current on its T2 filings and still be struck from its registry, and it can be in good standing at the registry while owing ten years of T2 returns.

So this count answers one of the two questions. The unfiled years checker answers the other.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many annual returns do I owe?

One for each tax year since the last one filed. The calculator above counts the tax year-ends that have passed.

Does a missed annual return create tax?

No. It creates a registry record that is out of date, and after enough missed years a corporation the registry treats as abandoned.

Does this tell me whether my T2 returns are filed?

No. The two trails are independent, so a clean registry record says nothing about the tax years and the reverse is also true.

What does the registry do after several missed years?

It can strike the corporation, dissolving it involuntarily. That ends the corporation’s legal existence and settles nothing at all on the tax side.

Is there a charge for each missed annual return?

The registry’s response is to strike the corporation rather than to charge it, which is a blunter consequence than a sum of money and has a different cure.

Does filing the outstanding ones put it right?

While the corporation is still on the register, yes: filing what is outstanding brings the record up to date. Once it has been struck, revival is the step that comes first.

Does this change what the Canada Revenue Agency is owed?

No. Tax years are counted on their own, and an unfiled T2 stays unfiled whatever the registry record happens to show.

I do not know when the last one was filed.

The registry record settles it, and it is the corporation’s own record to check. The calculator counts from the date you enter, so an uncertain date gives an uncertain count.

Does a change of directors count as one?

No. They are separate filings, and making one does not discharge the other even in the same year.

Is the count the same as the number of unfiled T2 returns?

Only by coincidence. One of each falls due for a tax year, but they are filed in different places, and a corporation is often current in one trail and years behind in the other.

title: Extra-Provincial Registration Checker | Which Registry Wants What
content:
Registry

Extra-Provincial Registration Checker

A corporation registered in more than one place owes each registry an annual return. Federal incorporation removes no provincial obligation.

Four answersRegistry by registryAT1 and CO-17 separateNone inside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Where the corporation is registered

Answer the four questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Each Registry Wants Its Own Annual Return

A federal corporation files an annual return with Corporations Canada for $12.00. An Ontario corporation files one through the Ontario Business Registry. A corporation registered in another province files with that jurisdiction’s registry.

A federally incorporated corporation operating in Ontario files both: the $12.00 Corporations Canada annual return and an Ontario filing. Federal incorporation does not remove the provincial obligation.

An Annual Return Is Not a Tax Return

JurisdictionIts own corporate income tax returnA registry annual return
AlbertaYes, the AT1Yes
QuebecYes, the CO-17Yes
OntarioNo, collected through the T2Yes, through the Ontario Business Registry
Every other province and territoryNo, collected through the T2Yes, with that jurisdiction’s registry

The provincial return requirement checker takes the income tax side on its own.

None of It Is Inside the Nil T2 Fee

Registry annual returns, the Alberta AT1 and the Quebec CO-17 are separate filings and are not included in the fee. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the federal nil T2 corporate tax return.

An annual return is not a tax filing, so having no income does not excuse it. So a dormant corporation registered in three places owes three annual returns and a T2, and none of the four satisfies any of the others.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does federal incorporation cover the provinces?

No. A federally incorporated corporation operating in Ontario files both the $12.00 Corporations Canada annual return and an Ontario filing. Federal incorporation does not remove the provincial obligation.

Is the Alberta AT1 an annual return?

No. Alberta administers its own corporate income tax, so the AT1 is a separate provincial income tax return. The same is true of the Quebec CO-17.

Are any of these inside the nil T2 fee?

No. Registry annual returns, the AT1 and the CO-17 are separate filings. The fee covers the federal nil T2 corporate tax return.

What is extra-provincial registration?

Registration in a province other than the one the corporation was incorporated in, which is what lets it carry on business there. Each registration brings that province’s own filings with it.

Does each registration mean another annual return?

Each registry asks for its own. Registration in more than one place means more than one annual return, each on its own registry’s cycle.

Does the Quebec CO-17 replace the T2?

No. Quebec administers its own corporate income tax, so the CO-17 is a separate provincial return filed in addition to the federal one.

Is a dormant corporation registered twice still filing twice?

Yes. An annual return reports who the directors are and where the office is rather than what was earned, so being dormant excuses neither registry.

What if the corporation no longer operates in the second province?

The registration stays on that registry, and its filings stay owed, until the registration itself is dealt with. Simply stopping work there ends nothing.

Does the $12.00 federal annual return cover the provinces?

No. The $12.00 Corporations Canada annual return is a federal filing, and a provincial registry is not a party to it.

Does registering in another province change the T2?

The federal return still covers the corporation as a whole. What changes is that a second province may want a return of its own, which is what the checker above names.

title: Corporate Revival Requirement Checker | Struck, Not Closed
content:
Registry

Corporate Revival Requirement Checker

Being struck by a registry is not a wind-up. What revival restores, and which tax years survived the striking.

Three answersStruck is not dissolvedTax years surviveRevival restores

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Where the corporation stands

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Struck Is Not Wound Up

A corporation struck by a registry for failing to file its annual return has not been wound up. It has been dissolved involuntarily, with its tax years still open and nothing settled.

A corporation found in this state is usually in it because the annual return lapsed, not because anyone decided to close it. The tax years are the part nobody looked at.

What the Striking Did and Did Not Do

WhatEffect of being struck
The corporation’s existenceEnded by the registry, and restorable by revival
The outstanding tax yearsSurvived the striking and are waiting
As a tax eventNot dissolution for tax purposes, and it cancels no outstanding T2 return
TradingIt cannot trade while struck

The post-dissolution return checker takes what is still owed afterwards, and the involuntary dissolution risk checker takes how a corporation gets here.

What Revival Is For

Registries provide for revival, which restores the corporation so the outstanding filings can be made and a proper wind-up completed.

So revival is the step that makes the rest possible rather than an end in itself. A corporation struck from a registry with unfiled tax years is in the worst of both positions: it cannot trade and it still owes returns. The dissolving versus filing nil every year comparison sets out what a completed wind-up ends.

Frequently Asked Questions

My corporation was struck off. Is it closed?

Not for tax purposes. It was dissolved involuntarily, with its tax years still open and nothing settled.

Did being struck cancel my outstanding T2 returns?

No. Being struck is not dissolution for tax purposes and it cancels no outstanding T2 return. The open years survived it.

What does revival do?

It restores the corporation so the outstanding filings can be made and a proper wind-up completed.

Can a struck corporation be revived at any time?

Each registry sets its own window and its own requirements, so it depends on the registry the corporation was struck from. That is the first thing to establish, and the registry is where to establish it.

Are the returns filed before revival or after?

Revival restores the corporation so that the filings can be made, so in practice it comes first. A dissolved corporation has no standing to put its years right.

Does revival create new tax years?

It restores the corporation rather than starting another one. The years that were open when it was struck are the same years afterwards.

Can it simply be left struck?

It can be left, but leaving it settles nothing. The open years stay open, and a clearance certificate cannot be issued while a return is outstanding.

Is a revived corporation the same corporation?

Yes. Revival restores the one that was struck, which is why its earlier tax years come back with it rather than falling away.

Does being struck stop the Canada Revenue Agency asking for returns?

No. The registry acted on its own account. An outstanding return stays outstanding, a demand to file one included.

Is revival part of nil T2 filing?

No. Revival is a registry step. Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the corporate returns, which are usually the reason the corporation is being revived at all.
